items.title: Kurumsal özrün anatomisi
items.text: An institutional apology can be read almost entirely from its grammar, and the reading is more reliable than any assessment of its sincerity. The decisive feature is who appears as the subject of the verb. Mistakes were made describes an event with no author; the passive has removed the one piece of information the sentence existed to supply. We are sorry that some people felt distressed relocates the harm into the perceptions of the injured party, and the word some quietly disputes the number. We apologize for any offense caused converts a specific act into a hypothetical one, since any is doing the work of admitting nothing in particular. These constructions are not accidents of style. They are produced by a process in which a legal department is asked to approve a text whose purpose is to accept responsibility, and the two aims are in direct conflict: an admission that satisfies the injured party is admissible in a court, and one that satisfies the lawyer does not satisfy anybody else. The organizations that have escaped this have generally done so by settling the legal question first and then writing the apology, which is expensive and looks from outside like the delay it is. What makes the subject worth examining is not the hypocrisy, which is ordinary, but the consistency. An apology's grammar predicts subsequent behavior better than its adjectives do. A statement naming an actor and an action is very often followed by a change in practice; a statement in which the harm happens by itself is very rarely followed by anything at all, and the people who received it usually knew that within a day of reading it. This is not a difficult test to apply and it requires no access to anybody's intentions. It can be run on a page of text in under a minute, which is a great deal more than can be said for most of what is written about corporate sincerity.

questions.q: What is the decisive feature of an apology?
options: Who appears as the subject of the verb
questions.note: "The decisive feature is who appears as the subject of the verb."

questions.q: What does 'mistakes were made' remove?
questions.note: "The passive has removed the one piece of information the sentence existed to supply."

questions.q: Why are these constructions produced?
options: A legal department approves a text meant to accept responsibility
questions.note: "A legal department is asked to approve a text whose purpose is to accept responsibility."

questions.q: How have some organizations escaped it?
options: By settling the legal question first
questions.note: "Settling the legal question first and then writing the apology."

questions.q: What does the grammar predict?
options: Whether a change in practice will follow
questions.note: "An apology's grammar predicts subsequent behavior better than its adjectives do."

items.title: Sanatta özgünlük sorusu
items.titleEn: The Value of Knowing Who Made It
items.text: When a painting long attributed to a major figure is reassigned to a workshop assistant, its price collapses and its appearance does not change by a single brushstroke. The usual response to this is amused contempt for a market that has confused an object with a signature. The contempt is too quick. Some of the value that disappears is indeed speculative, but a considerable part of it is informational, and the information is genuinely lost. A work by a known artist sits inside an account of a life: it can be dated, placed among other works, read as a development of something earlier or a retreat from it. Reassigned to an unnamed assistant, the same canvas becomes an object about which almost nothing further can be said, and the loss is real even for a viewer who has never thought about money. There is a second consideration that complicates the picture further. A great deal of art made before the nineteenth century was produced by workshops in which the master's contribution might be a design, a face, or a supervisory glance, and the modern demand for a single author imposes a category that the objects themselves do not support. Museums have handled this with increasing honesty, replacing confident labels with descriptions of what is actually known. Auction houses have not, because the ambiguity has no price. The most interesting consequence is what happens to the demoted painting itself. A canvas that hung for eighty years as a minor work by a major figure is frequently seen for the first time, by curators and visitors alike, on the day it stops being one. Until then it was read through the name, and everything in it that did not fit the name was either not noticed or quietly explained as a weak passage. Removed from that account, the picture has to be looked at, and a surprising number of such works turn out to reward the attention, which is an argument for the reassignment that almost nobody making it bothers to use.

questions.q: What does not change when a work is reassigned?
questions.note: "Its appearance does not change by a single brushstroke."

questions.q: What kind of value is genuinely lost?
questions.note: "A considerable part of it is informational, and the information is genuinely lost."

questions.q: What does a known artist's work sit inside?
questions.note: "A work by a known artist sits inside an account of a life."

questions.q: What does the modern demand for a single author do?
options: Imposes a category the objects do not support
questions.note: "Imposes a category that the objects themselves do not support."

questions.q: What happens to the demoted painting?
options: It is often really seen for the first time
questions.note: Son cümle.

items.title: Alışkanlığın kırılma anı
items.titleEn: The Window That Opens When Life Changes
items.text: Behavior that has resisted every deliberate effort at change frequently alters by itself when a person moves house, starts a job or has a child. The finding is robust and its explanation is uncomfortable for anyone who believes that habits are primarily a matter of will. A habit is held in place not by the desire to perform it but by a stable set of cues: the same route, the same kitchen, the same people at the same hour. Remove the cues and the behavior loses its support, which is why a smoker who has failed eleven times may succeed in the month of a relocation without any additional resolve. The practical implication is that the moment matters more than the method, and that the moments are few, brief and unannounced. Public health programmes have begun to act on this, targeting the weeks around a move or a birth rather than January, with results that exceed anything achieved by conventional campaigns. The same mechanism has an unwelcome symmetry that the literature discusses less. Disruption removes the support for good habits too. A person who exercised reliably for six years may simply stop on changing job, not through any decision but because the route home no longer passes the pool, and will often describe the change as a loss of motivation, which is an explanation that locates in the character something that happened in the street. Anybody planning a large change would do better to spend an hour asking which of their current habits are being held up by the arrangement they are about to dismantle. The exercise is short and almost nobody performs it, because the behaviors in question are invisible precisely to the degree that they are working. A person can list every intention they have failed to keep and will rarely think to list the walk they have taken four times a week for six years without once deciding to.

questions.q: What holds a habit in place?
questions.note: "A habit is held in place not by the desire to perform it but by a stable set of cues."

questions.q: Why might a smoker succeed during a move?
questions.note: "Remove the cues and the behavior loses its support."

questions.q: What are public health programs now targeting?
options: The weeks around a move or a birth
questions.note: "Targeting the weeks around a move or a birth rather than January."

questions.q: What is the unwelcome symmetry?
options: Disruption removes support for good habits too
questions.note: "Disruption removes the support for good habits too."

questions.q: What does the writer recommend before a large change?
options: Ask which behaviors depend on the current arrangement
questions.note: Son cümle.

items.title: Yardımın koşulları
items.text: Aid given with conditions attached has an obvious justification and a less obvious record. The justification is that money handed over without requirements may be spent badly, and there is no shortage of cases in which it was. The record is that the conditions themselves consume a substantial fraction of the value transferred. A grant requiring quarterly reporting in a specified format obliges the receiving body to employ somebody to produce those reports, and where the receiving body is a clinic with fourteen staff the post is filled by taking a person away from the work the grant was meant to support. Where several donors each impose their own format, the administrative load can exceed the marginal benefit of the later grants entirely, a threshold that is crossed silently and is visible only to the people filling in the forms. The research on unconditional transfers is now substantial and its findings are consistently uncomfortable for the sector. Money handed directly to households, with no instruction about its use, is spent on much what an economist would predict and much what the recipients would say if asked: school fees, a roof, a stock of goods to sell. The predicted waste is measurable and small. This has not produced the change in practice that the evidence would justify, and the reason is worth stating plainly. A donor who transfers money without conditions has also transferred the decision, and with it the ability to describe what the money achieved. The conditions were never only about the risk of waste. They were about retaining the authorship of the outcome, which is a legitimate thing for a donor to want and a poor reason to make a clinic hire an administrator. There is a middle position that some funders have reached and that is rarely described, perhaps because it sounds like a retreat. They attach no conditions to the spending and heavy conditions to the reporting of outcomes, which leaves the decision where it belongs and keeps the donor able to say what happened. It costs the recipient a form at the end rather than a post for the duration.

questions.q: What do the conditions consume?
options: A substantial fraction of the value transferred
questions.note: "The conditions themselves consume a substantial fraction of the value transferred."

questions.q: What happens in a clinic with fourteen staff?
options: Somebody is taken away from the work to file reports
questions.note: "The post is filled by taking a person away from the work the grant was meant to support."

questions.q: What can happen when several donors impose formats?
options: The load exceeds the benefit of later grants
questions.note: "The administrative load can exceed the marginal benefit of the later grants."

questions.q: What does research on unconditional transfers find?
questions.note: "The predicted waste is measurable and small."

questions.q: What were the conditions really about?
questions.note: "They were about retaining the authorship of the outcome."

items.title: Bilginin tarihi
items.titleEn: The Footnote and What It Promises
items.text: The footnote is a small and strange invention whose function is frequently misunderstood. It is generally taken to be a device for giving credit, and it does that, but its older and more important purpose is to make a claim checkable by a stranger. A sentence with a reference attached says something the sentence alone cannot: that the author is prepared to be found wrong by anybody willing to walk to a library. This is a considerable commitment and it explains a pattern that otherwise looks merely pedantic. Disciplines with dense referencing are not more honest than those without; they are differently exposed, and the exposure disciplines the writing in ways that survive even where nobody checks. The habit has weakened for reasons that have nothing to do with intellectual decline. A link rots. A reference to a database that has been reorganized points at nothing, and a claim supported by a source the reader cannot reach is functionally an assertion. Archival projects address part of this and are chronically underfunded, since preserving the ability to check a claim made in 2009 has no constituency and produces nothing anybody can announce. What has largely disappeared, and is worth naming because its loss is invisible, is the negative footnote: the note that says a plausible alternative was considered and rejected, and why. It costs an author something to write, since it names a possibility the reader might not otherwise have thought of and invites them to weigh it. Its absence is not detectable by any reader, which is precisely what makes its presence informative about the person who wrote it. An author who includes such notes is telling a reader that the argument was contested in private before it was published, and that the version on the page survived the contest. No formal system can require this, and any attempt to require it would produce a hundred thousand notes rejecting alternatives nobody seriously held.

questions.q: What is the footnote's older purpose?
options: To make a claim checkable by a stranger
questions.note: "Its older and more important purpose is to make a claim checkable by a stranger."

questions.q: What does a reference commit the author to?
options: Being found wrong by anybody who looks
questions.note: "The author is prepared to be found wrong by anybody willing to walk to a library."

questions.q: How does the writer describe densely referenced fields?
questions.note: "They are differently exposed."

questions.q: What has weakened the habit?
options: Links and databases that no longer resolve
questions.note: "A link rots. A reference to a database that has been reorganized points at nothing."

questions.q: What is the negative footnote?
options: A note saying an alternative was considered and rejected
questions.note: "The note that says a plausible alternative was considered and rejected, and why."
